angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 667,872 km at 54.35 pc = 0.16 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 18.3997 +/- 0.0150 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 54.35 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.96 solar radii from Vidotto et al. (2014), MNRAS 441, 2361, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729): 667,872 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.983 (0.942 to 1.023) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5820 K from Waite et al. (2015), MNRAS 449, 8, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729). Spin inclination 62 degrees and rotation period 2.32 d from Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2, the values of the ZDI inversion (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Waite et al. (2015), MNRAS 449, 8, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-29615.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.466, rounded to two decimals
